title: Safety and security of large language models in healthcare.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: no PMCID, not open access in Europe PMC, no supplement, no accessions in text or text-mined, no NCBI links (GEO/SRA/BioProject), no Zenodo/Dryad hits on the DOI. Abstract only.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The abstract says this is a literature review: it maps security hazards and safety layers for LLMs (large language models) in healthcare. No dataset, measurements or label table is described.

a1_downloadable.note: No data exists to download: this is a review article, and the repository and accession search found nothing (checked via paper_context.py).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no measured label. Any threat taxonomy in the review would be the authors' qualitative classification, not a column of measured outcomes.

a3_inputs_present.note: No inputs: the review has no feature table.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label exists; a review-derived threat classification would be expert opinion, not a physical measurement.

honest_claim_h3: None possible: the paper provides no data from which a model could learn anything.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use descriptions of attacks on medical chatbots to predict how clinically relevant each threat is.
plain_idea.train_on: Threats catalogued in the review, each described in text; number of examples unknown and likely only dozens.
plain_idea.predict: The authors' rating of each threat's current clinical relevance, which is an expert judgement, not a measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Not worthwhile: the labels are opinions on a small hand-built list, so a model would just copy the authors' judgement.

ml_idea: None viable. This is a narrative and systematic review of LLM (large language model) safety in healthcare, with no deposited dataset.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no data.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already done: paper_context.py found no supplement, accessions or repository records for this review.

verdict_reason: This is a review article on LLM (large language model) safety in healthcare. It is also outside biology, and it has no dataset, no supplement and no repository deposit, so Part A1 and A2 fail.
